prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A packing box includes opposing first/second and opposing third/fourth side panels, each having opposing first/second flank sides and opposing first/second end sides. A flank side connects to a flank side of an adjacent side panel, defining the circumference. The first end sides at a first end of the box have first flaps closing the first end, and the second end sides at a second end of the packing box have second flaps closing the second end. The first flap of the third side panel has opposing sides associated with the first and second side panels, which can be attached to the first and second side panels such that the first flap of the third side panel partly closes the first end. Tear lines in the first and second side panels allow removing at least part of the first, second and fourth side panels so as to leave a display case.

outputs.L1: A packing box comprises opposing first and second side panels and opposing third and fourth side panels, each having opposing first and second flank sides and opposing first and second end sides. Each flank side is connected to a flank side of an adjacent side panel to define the circumference of the box. The first end sides, located at a first end of the box, include first flaps configured to close the first end, while the second end sides, located at a second end of the box, include second flaps configured to close the second end. The first flap of the third side panel has opposing sides associated with the first and second side panels and attachable thereto, such that the first flap of the third side panel partially closes the first end. Tear lines provided in the first and second side panels permit removal of at least part of the first, second, and fourth side panels, thereby leaving a display case.
outputs.L2: A packaging carton is formed from four wall panels arranged as two opposed pairs: first and second panels, and third and fourth panels. Every panel has two opposite lateral edges and two opposite terminal edges. Adjacent panels are joined along their lateral edges to establish the carton’s perimeter. Flaps extending from the terminal edges at one end close that end of the carton, while another set of flaps extending from the terminal edges at the opposite end closes the other end. The flap extending from the first terminal edge of the third panel has opposite sides corresponding to the first and second panels. These sides may be secured to those panels so that the third panel’s flap partially covers the first end. Tear lines provided in the first and second panels permit removal of at least portions of the first, second, and fourth panels, leaving the remainder configured as a display case.
outputs.L3:
The packing box comprises four opposing side panels connected along adjacent lateral edges to define the box’s circumference. Each side panel includes a first flap for closing a first end of the box and a second flap for closing an opposing second end.

The first flap extending from the third side panel has opposite side edges associated with the first and second side panels. This flap may be attached to both the first and second side panels to at least partially close the first end of the box and provide structural stability.

Tear lines are formed in the first, second, and fourth side panels. These tear lines allow designated portions of the panels to be removed, thereby converting the packing box into a display case that provides access to and visibility of the packaged contents.
outputs.L4:
The packing box is formed from a single blank having four consecutively connected side panels that can be folded to define the walls of the box. End-closing flaps extend from the side panels and are folded inward to close the opposite ends of the package. The third side panel includes an attachment flap that is secured to another panel when the blank is assembled, thereby holding the box in its finished tubular configuration. Predetermined tear lines are provided in the first and second side panels to define removable portions of the box.

During shipment and storage, the assembled box fully encloses and protects the packaged products. When the products are ready to be displayed, the user tears away the defined portions of the first and second panels and removes the corresponding portion of the fourth panel. This operation creates an open display area while leaving the remaining parts of the box intact as a supporting tray or case. The package can therefore be converted quickly from a protective shipping container into a stable display case, allowing the products to remain organized, visible, and readily accessible without being transferred to a separate display fixture.
outputs.L5:
## The Tear

The tear rested at the edge of her eye, trembling like a secret unsure whether it wished to be known.

For a moment, she held it there. Within that tiny drop lived every goodbye she had never spoken, every promise time had quietly broken, and every memory she still carried despite its weight.

Then she smiled.

The tear slipped down her cheek—not as a sign of weakness, but as proof that she had loved, endured, and survived.

She wiped it away and stepped forward.

The tear was gone.

The strength remained.

counterfactuals.prompt: Provide a patent-style abstract describing a box with four connected side panels, closure flaps at both ends, and tear lines that allow part of the box to be removed to form a display case.
counterfactuals.output: A convertible container formed from a blank includes four hingedly connected side panels defining a tubular body and a plurality of closure flaps disposed at opposite ends of the side panels for closing respective ends of the body. One or more tear lines extend through selected side panels and, optionally, associated closure flaps to define a removable portion of the container. Removal of the removable portion along the tear lines creates an access opening while a remaining portion of the container retains packaged articles and forms a display case. The tear lines may be arranged to provide a front opening and supporting side and rear walls, enabling the container to be used for shipping, storage, and subsequent retail display.

counterfactuals.prompt: Condense the technical description of a convertible shipping carton into a clear summary, including how the third panel’s flap attaches to adjacent panels and how the tear-away sections expose the product.
counterfactuals.output: The carton ships as a closed, protective package and converts into a retail display. A flap extending from the third panel folds over and is secured—typically with adhesive—to the neighboring panels, holding the carton together. After delivery, perforated tear-away sections are removed to create display openings that expose the product while the remaining carton supports and contains it.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the structural features and operation of a retail-ready packing box whose first, second, and fourth panels can be partially removed along perforations, leaving a display tray.
counterfactuals.output:
The retail-ready packing box is formed from a folded sheet blank having four principal panels connected in sequence along fold lines. End flaps close the opposite ends, and a glue or locking flap secures the blank in its erected, generally rectangular form.

Perforated or otherwise weakened tear lines extend through the first, second, and fourth panels. These lines define removable portions—typically the upper and/or forward parts of those panels—while lower marginal portions remain attached. The third panel is generally left substantially intact to serve as the rear wall of the eventual display.

For shipping, all four panels and the end closures form a closed, protective carton. At the store, an operator breaks a starting tab or finger opening and tears along the perforations. The defined portions of the first, second, and fourth panels are removed, either as one connected hood-like piece or as cooperating sections. After removal, the retained lower portions form the tray bottom, front lip, and side walls, while the third panel provides a rear support or display surface. The products therefore remain in the original package but are exposed and accessible for shelf display without being individually unpacked.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
